source.title: How green is the grass on the other side? Frontopolar cortex and the evidence in favor of alternative courses of action.

confidence_rationale: Direct fMRI evidence that FPC represents the value of the foregone/unchosen alternative -- establishing the retained-alternative substrate is biologically real (supports) -- but as a transient online comparison signal, which is exactly the SD-033e/MECH-264 cfv_now scalar form; so it also CONFIRMS the gap (no persistence of WHICH alternative past the decision) that MECH-486 must fill. Direction therefore mixed.
failure_signatures: FPC's signal is a running relative-advantage magnitude, not an identity-and-persistence store; a retention design that assumes the biological substrate already keeps 'which alternative, past the tick' over-reads this result -- it does not.

The representation is tied to the moment of comparison/switching; absent a dedicated persistence mechanism the alternative's identity is not available for later retrospective counterfactual evaluation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Frontopolar cortex tracks the relative advantage in favour of switching to a foregone alternative when choices are made voluntarily; FPC functional connectivity changes when subjects decide to switch, and interindividual FPC signal variation predicts behavioural adaptation, while vmPFC encodes the value of the current decision.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the biological anchor for REE's SD-033e/MECH-264 frontopolar counterfactual-value (cfv_now) mechanism: representing the value of the rejected alternative is real and adaptive. But the signal is an ONLINE relative-advantage magnitude tied to the comparison/switch moment -- it matches cfv_now's 'transient scalar overwritten every tick' form and does NOT carry which alternative, persisting past the decision. So Boorman 2009 simultaneously supports 'a rejected-alternative value substrate exists' and sharpens MECH-486's novelty: retaining WHICH alternative existed, past the tick, for later evaluation, is the thing this literature does not provide.
mapping.mapping_caveat: fMRI BOLD of a value/advantage magnitude during two-armed choice; it speaks to representing the foregone option's value at decision time, not to storing its identity or trajectory for retrospective use. Reading persistence into it would be an over-transfer.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults; fMRI; voluntary two-alternative reward learning with a Bayesian RL model; frontopolar and ventromedial prefrontal cortex.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality, much-replicated fMRI finding and the direct anchor for MECH-264. Mapping_fidelity strong for 'foregone-value substrate exists'; the mixed direction is deliberate -- it confirms the transient-scalar form and thus the persistence gap.
